clue.text: Cat's paw not small enough?

parts.note: read with the question mark, 'not small enough' means too large, so this gives the word too
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large, the opposite of small

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a cat's foot is too large, as if sizing it up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'not small enough' as 'too large': TOO plus L for large.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's paw is a person used by another to do their dirty work, an instrument or dupe.

clue.text: Marksman in military show is German

parts.note: a tattoo is an evening military display with music and marching
ist is the German word for 'is'

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter performing at an army pageant turns out to be German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marksman' is not a shooter here but someone who makes marks on skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a body artist literally makes marks, inking designs into skin.

clue.text: Round relative sheds pound in weight

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: sheds means the pound letter is dropped from the rest

parts.note: an uncle is a family relative
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: A plump relative loses a pound of body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperial unit of mass, one sixteenth of a pound avoirdupois.

clue.text: Critical moment — time to take picture?

definitions.meaning: the point at which a situation erupts into crisis
playfully, the moment when a camera's flash goes off

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the instant trouble ignites, and whimsically the instant a photo is taken with flash.

clue.text: Machine-wrecker diluted fluid

indicators.note: fluid means flowing and changeable, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone smashing machines has watered-down liquid on their hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The original Luddites were 19th-century English textile workers who smashed mechanised looms.

clue.text: To that extent permitted to harass for cash

parts.note: so means to that degree
licit means lawful, allowed

explanation.surface: Pestering people for money is allowed only up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to accost or importune people, as for money or business.

clue.text: One to drag feet moving on airport carts

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: A slowcoach dawdles while pushing luggage trolleys around a terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who drags their feet keeps putting things off, a habitual delayer.

clue.text: One can rave about eastern traveller

indicators.note: about here means next to, so the eastern letter sits up against the rave

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tin is a can
to rant is to rave

explanation.surface: A wanderer is perfectly able to sound off about the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who journeys from place to place, a wanderer with no fixed home.

clue.text: Cool, cold and dry outside in shade

indicators.note: outside means the dry letters go round the rest

parts.note: TT means teetotal, i.e. dry
in means fashionable, cool
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone describes ideal weather for sitting in the shade: cool, cold and dry outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' is TT, the teetotal abbreviation, not a weather word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint or tinge of colour, a slight shade.

clue.text: Average person entertains them extravagantly

indicators.note: extravagantly means wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An ordinary person lavishly hosts some guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for the ordinary citizen whose views are typical of the public.

clue.text: Irish MP sent around capital endlessly seeking a quantity of beer

indicators.note: sent around means the MP letters are wrapped round the capital

parts.note: TD (Teachta Dála) is a member of the Irish parliament

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Ankara is the capital of Turkey

explanation.surface: An Irish politician is despatched round a city looking for some beer.
explanation.walkthrough: A TD is a member of the Dáil, the Irish lower house.
explanation.definitionFit: A large drinking mug, and by extension the amount of beer it holds.

clue.text: National starter refused, ruining Thai neighbour

indicators.note: ruining means wrecking, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the first letter of the word is turned away

explanation.surface: A local cook spoils a Thai dish for a neighbour by refusing the starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter refused' drops N from NATIONAL, leaving ATIONAL; 'ruining' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Laos borders Thailand, so a person from Laos is a Thai's neighbour.

clue.text: Bookmarks put back in Vile Bodies

indicators.note: put back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone replaces markers in a copy of Evelyn Waugh's novel Vile Bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters ILEBO sitting in 'Vile Bodies'; 'put back' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are dagger-shaped symbols printed in books to mark passages or footnotes.

clue.text: Wrong to have Irish soldiers pressing NCO at court

indicators.note: pressing means squeezing round, so the NCO sits inside

parts.note: non-commissioned officer, taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, an army corps

explanation.surface: It is wrong for Irish troops to lean on a sergeant at a court martial.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean mistaken or not right.

clue.text: Overnight case?

parts.note: not a small suitcase but a hospital case, a patient staying the night on the ward

explanation.walkthrough: 'Overnight case' suggests luggage; here the case is a medical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient admitted to stay in hospital at least overnight, unlike an outpatient.

clue.text: Drunk bishop in to serve old Soviet executive

indicators.note: in means the drunk bishop goes inside the serving word

parts.note: to pour is to serve a drink
lit is slang for drunk
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A tipsy bishop is installed to serve on an old Soviet ruling body.
explanation.definitionFit: The policy-making committee of the Soviet Communist Party.

clue.text: Flat flake almost touches soft skin on head

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is left off

parts.note: a scale is a thin flat flake, as on a fish
P is the musical abbreviation piano, soft

explanation.surface: Dandruff on the head: flaky skin comes off softly.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin covering the top of the head, where hair grows.

clue.text: Ancestors are not wrapped in sheet

indicators.note: wrapped in means these letters go inside the sheet word

parts.note: a page is a sheet of paper
NT is short for not, as in n't

explanation.surface: Forebears are not shrouded in sheets, a remark about ghosts or burial.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lineage or descent, the parents and forebears one comes from.

clue.text: Material litter lout occasionally scatters

indicators.note: scatters means the chosen letters are strewn into a new order
occasionally means taking only every other letter

explanation.surface: A litter lout now and then drops scraps of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes LTELU from 'litter lout'; 'scatters' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine net fabric used for veils and ballet tutus.

clue.text: Coolest times New Testament suggests?

parts.note: NT is short for New Testament, and those two letters are the middle of the word winter

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the New Testament says about the coldest seasons.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: NT sits at the middle of WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The depths of winter around the solstice, the coldest stretch of the year.

clue.text: Work unit: when second part arrives, first arrives too?

definitions.meaning: a measure of labour, one person working for sixty minutes

definitions.text: when second part arrives, first arrives too?
definitions.meaning: a play on the saying that the hour brings forth the person: when the hour comes, the man comes

explanation.surface: A puzzle about one part of something following another.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit measuring work done by one worker in sixty minutes; the second reading splits it into its two words.

clue.text: Most expensive honey

definitions.meaning: the costliest, the superlative of pricey

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the costliest, and a loving form of address like darling.

clue.text: Sicilian city comes around to unresponsive state

indicators.note: comes around means the city wraps round the next word

parts.note: Catania is a city on the east coast of Sicily

explanation.surface: Someone visiting a Sicilian city is coming round from a stupor.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition of stupor or immobility in which a person does not react.

clue.text: Hold on tight having caught fish

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ling is a long-bodied sea fish

explanation.surface: An angler grips the rod after hooking a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to grip firmly and not let go.

clue.text: Stove lit for second time

parts.note: an Aga is a make of cast-iron range cooker
a fire that is in is still lit

explanation.surface: The stove has been lit a second time after going out.
explanation.definitionFit: Once more, on a second occasion.

clue.text: Emerge missing second line in dramatic role

indicators.note: missing means the second letter is removed

parts.note: to arise is to emerge

explanation.surface: An actor forgets a line when stepping on stage in a role.
explanation.definitionFit: The airy spirit serving Prospero in Shakespeare's The Tempest, a stage part.

clue.text: Changed routine yet to be delivered

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An altered schedule means a parcel has not arrived yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for in the womb, describing a baby before birth.

clue.text: Time invested in symphony and certain literature

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside the symphony

parts.note: Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony

explanation.surface: Someone spends time on a symphony and a particular kind of book.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexually explicit writing, one particular category of literature.

clue.text: Author secretly wore tights to dance

indicators.note: to dance means the letters are jigged into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A writer covertly put on tights to go dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To write a work that is published under another person's name, authoring it in secret.

clue.text: Ships ultimately abandoned: take flight

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a fleet is a group of ships

explanation.surface: Sailors desert their ships at last and run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away from danger, to escape.
